bug_semantics: Apache Airflow EnvironmentVariablesBackend stored a team-scoped Connection or Variable as AIRFLOW_CONN__<TEAM>___<ID> / AIRFLOW_VAR__<TEAM>___<ID>. get_variable/get_conn_value probed only the caller's own namespace and then fell through to os.environ.get(PREFIX + id.upper()). Supplying the encoded identifier _<TEAM>___<ID> made that global read byte-identical to another team's namespaced variable. A later guard, _is_team_specific_accessed_as_global, was supposed to stop this but only ran when team_name is None and used re.fullmatch(r'_[^_]+___.+', secret_id), which cannot span a legal underscore-bearing team name (^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{3,50}$). With the guard inapplicable, an authenticated user of one team could have POST /api/v2/connections/test call Connection.get_connection_from_secrets(connection_id) and authenticate outward with the other team's credentials. Exploitation requires [core] multi_team, [core] test_connection=Enabled (ships Disabled), team-scoped secrets in the API-server environment, and knowledge of the encoded identifier.
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism was first written in PR #58905 member d3033106035253962a8b264d06dfa1dcc988a840 (GitHub-squashed to main as d32091cd4f4b2b0935bc71e02e2995cdb8713a30): get_variable gained a team-scoped AIRFLOW_VAR__<TEAM>___<KEY> probe plus an unconditional global PREFIX+key read, with no refusal of a namespaced id. PR #59476 copied the same fall-through into get_conn_value (the connections/test sink). PR #62588 later added the incomplete guard; it is attempted remediation, not the first write. Author/committer of the BIC is human vincbeck; the commit object has no AI trailers.
